cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: to introduce the topic and clarify key target vocabulary for the session.

cosy-slide.cosy-instruction: Review the key vocabulary for this session below:

cosy-blockquote.p: Longing – a strong wish for something or someone.

p.em: Example: He felt a deep longing to return to his childhood home.

cosy-blockquote.p: Melancholy – a feeling of pensive sadness, typically with no obvious cause.

p.em: Example: The rainy afternoon filled her with a sense of gentle melancholy.

cosy-blockquote.p: Untranslatable – not able to be expressed in another language.

p.em: Example: Many Portuguese speakers believe that 'saudade' is completely untranslatable.

cosy-blockquote.p: La nostalgia ≠ La modernidad – sentimiento de pena por la lejanía o el tiempo pasado ≠ cualidad de lo moderno o actual.

p.em: Example: Sintió una profunda nostalgia por el pueblo antiguo, un contraste total con la fría modernidad.

cosy-blockquote.p: Wistful – having or showing a feeling of vague or regretful longing.

p.em: Example: She gave a wistful smile as she remembered her days at university.

cosy-blockquote.p: Evocative – bringing strong images, memories, or feelings to mind.

p.em: Example: The smell of lavender was highly evocative of her grandmother's garden.

cosy-blockquote.p: Bittersweet – arousing pleasure tinged with sadness or pain.

p.em: Example: It was a bittersweet moment when they said goodbye at the airport.

cosy-blockquote.p: Poignant – evoking a keen sense of sadness or regret.

p.em: Example: The film's ending was incredibly poignant and left the audience in tears.

cosy-blockquote.p: Ephemeral – lasting for a very short time.

p.em: Example: The beauty of the sunset is ephemeral, fading within minutes.

cosy-blockquote.p: Resonance – the quality in a sound or image of being deep, full, and reverberating.

p.em: Example: His words had a deep emotional resonance with everyone in the room.

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: pair/group discussion on core session themes.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs or small breakout groups, discuss the following questions:

ol.li:
What is the specific object of your longing when you feel homesick or lonely?
★ When was the last time you had to confront longing in your own personal journey?

How does listening to certain music evoke a sense of melancholy in your soul?
★ How comfortable are you with allowing melancholy to guide your daily decisions?

Why do you think some emotions are untranslatable across different cultures?
★ Have you ever felt a deep sense of conflict regarding untranslatable in a relationship?

Is nostalgia always a positive feeling, or can it prevent us from living in the present?
★ Can you share a moment from your childhood where la nostalgia felt completely natural?

When was the last time you felt wistful while looking at old family photographs?
★ How do you personally nurture wistful when you feel emotionally exhausted?

Which smells or tastes are most evocative of your childhood home?
★ Have you ever had to choose between social conformity and personal evocative?

Why are bittersweet endings in movies often more memorable than happy ones?
★ Who in your life best embodies the essence of bittersweet, and what have they taught you?

Can you share a poignant moment from your life that completely changed your perspective?
★ In what area of your life do you feel poignant is most desperately needed right now?

How does the ephemeral nature of life make our experiences more valuable?
★ How has your personal understanding of ephemeral shifted over the last five years?

How can a simple word have such a deep resonance across different generations?
★ If you had to describe your personal experience with resonance in one word, what would it be?

cosy-teacher-notes.p: Stage aim: deeper debate and statement evaluation in pairs/groups.

cosy-slide.cosy-group-instruction: In pairs, debate and state whether you agree or disagree with these statements:

ol.li:
In the future, technology will enable us to digitize and share our experience of longing directly. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How would you personally adapt if longing became entirely obsolete in tomorrow's world?

The rapid speed of modern society will eventually make melancholy an obsolete concept. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you be willing to use technology to artificially boost your capacity for melancholy?

Future educational systems will prioritize the cultivation of untranslatable over traditional academic skills. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you want future generations of your family to remember your relationship with untranslatable?

As artificial intelligence advances, machines will exhibit a superior capacity for la nostalgia compared to humans. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could design a futuristic school, how would you teach the value of la nostalgia to children?

In the coming decades, wistful will become a highly commercialized luxury commodity. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Do you fear a future where wistful is fully managed or monitored by digital algorithms?

The survival of human civilization will depend on our collective ability to practice evocative. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ How do you personally prepare for a future where evocative is increasingly rare?

Future generations will look back at our current understanding of bittersweet with deep skepticism. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If you could send a single message about bittersweet to people living 100 years in the future, what would it be?

Global digital connectivity will make true poignant incredibly difficult to maintain in the future. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ Would you choose to live in a futuristic utopia that completely guarantees poignant at the cost of your freedom?

In the future, social status will be determined by a person's capacity for ephemeral rather than wealth. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ What role do you hope ephemeral will play in your own personal future over the next decade?

A world fully governed by logic will have no space left for the mystery of resonance. : Do you agree or disagree?
★ If a machine could perfectly replicate your experience of resonance, would you still value it?

ul.li: Incorrect: I am feeling nostalgia → Correct: I feel nostalgia / I'm feeling nostalgic ((Noun vs Adjective))
Incorrect: The book is very poignant for me → Correct: The book is very poignant / The book really resonates with me ((Usage of poignant))
Incorrect: It is depend of the person → Correct: It depends on the person ((Structure and preposition))
Incorrect: I am agree with you → Correct: I agree with you ((Verb agreement))
Incorrect: It is depend on you → Correct: It depends on you ((Verb vs Adjective))
